sources.entry: Genea.app - Genealogy tool designed with privacy in mind that anyone can use to author or edit their family tree. Data is stored in the GEDCOM format and all processing is done in the browser. (Source Code) MIT Javascript

summary.one_liner: Genea is a browser-based genealogy app for visually building and editing family trees, storing data in the GEDCOM format with no server-side components.
summary.what_it_does: Genea lets users visually build and edit a family tree online. It reads and writes genealogy data in GEDCOM format, and all processing happens in the browser without server-side components. The family tree is drawn with the Graphviz library compiled to WebAssembly, using a default layout that includes grandparents, parents, partners, siblings and children. An abstraction layer assigns data to tree nodes. The README says the app can be unpacked and served over HTTPS for self-hosting, or used via the hosted Genea.app website. It also describes optionally storing GEDCOM files in a Git host such as Gitea or GitLab, or GitHub, to sync across devices.
use_cases: build a family tree in the browser
self-host a private family tree app
store family history data in Git
how_to_run: Unpack the files into a directory
notable: No server-side components; all processing runs in the browser
Stores data directly as GEDCOM 5.5.5 files
Graphviz compiled to WebAssembly draws the tree
Allows a FAM record to contain two HUSB or two WIFE records to support same-sex marriages, a deliberate deviation from the standard
caveats: Only spouse, parent, child and sibling-style relationships are supported; other relationship types are not, since GEDCOM lacks a gender-neutral partner record
Self-hosting is recommended over HTTPS to control the version run
Syncing across devices requires an external Git host of the user's choice
